listings.name: Al Ahmadiya School and Heritage House
listings.content: Built in 1912, Al Ahmadiya School was Dubai's first school and has now been nicely restored. It would be a stretch to call the exhibits of old reed pens and diplomas fascinating, but they've tried pretty hard, and if nothing else, the air-con and clean toilets may come in handy. The attached heritage house is a traditional Emirati-style home built in the 1890s.

listings.name: Deira Clocktower
listings.content: A landmark of Deira and important as a monument built before the independence of UAE.
listings.address: Abu Baker Al Siddiqe Rd 110 crossing Al Maktoum Rd 105

listings.name: Dhow Wharfage
listings.content: The dhows ply the Arabian Sea and the Indian Ocean, transporting goods between south and south-west Asia and east Africa.
listings.address: Baniyas Rd, Rigga Al Buteen community 125

listings.name: Mamzar Park
listings.content: You can swim at Al Mamzar Beach or stroll in the park. Though less popular than other Dubai parks, it has its share of Dubai's greenery. Monday & Wednesday for women only.
listings.address: 104 Al Khaleej Rd, Al Mamzar community

listings.name: Dubai Municipality Museum
listings.address: Old Baladiya St crossing Al Souk Al Kabeer St, Al Buteen community

listings.name: Women's Museum
listings.content: Highlight the contribution of women to UAE's economy, culture and politic for the independence in the 1960s and since. Life of great women and daily life of Emirati people. An exhibit is also dedicated to the famous Emirati female poet Ousha bint Khalifa Suwidi.
listings.address: 28 St, Al Dhagaya community, P.O. Box 1086

listings.name: Naif Police Museum
listings.address: 106 Naif Rd crossing 9A St, Naif community

listings.name: Gold Price Checking - Dubai Souq
listings.content: Before purchasing gold in Dubai’s famous Gold Souk, it's always best to check the current live gold prices. Gold prices fluctuate daily due to global market trends. Visit [GoldRateUAE](https://goldrateuae.ae/) to get the latest price updates. Prices here are available for various gold types including 22K, 24K, and 18K gold.
listings.price: Prices vary based on market rate

listings.name: Cinecity - Al Ghurair Centre
listings.content: The largest cinema chain in the Middle East. It is a part of Novo Cinemas group. This 8-screen cinema complex including 14 anchor stores has 2 levels.
listings.address: Al Ghurair City, Al Riqqah St

listings.name: VOX Deira City Centre
listings.content: VOX has 11 screens with various types of experiences for movie lovers. The immersive experience of DepthQ 3D technology, fully reclining seats, VIP seats, 20-m screens and brightest and clearest pictures is their latest addition.

listings.name: Dubai Creek Golf & Yacht Club
listings.content: This leisure hub is an ideal destination for golfers. It provides wide-ranging set of services, floodlit par-3 course, modern golf academies and driving ranges. Visitors can enjoy a challenging game of golf, hire a private boat to enjoy the calm waters or take a swim.
listings.address: Radisson Blu Hotel, Dubai Deira Creek, Bani Yas Rd, 476

listings.name: Dinner Dhow Cruises
listings.content: A 2-hour dhow cruise tour on a "5-star" dhow, along Dubai Creek with commentary in English.
listings.address: Pier 1 in Dhow Wharfage, Baniyas Rd, Rigga Al Buteen community

listings.name: Jungle Bay Waterpark
listings.content: Brand new waterpark, as of April 2021.
listings.address: Le Meridien Mina Seyahi Beach Resort & Marina

listings.name: Bhatkal Restaurant
listings.content: An Indian restaurant

listings.name: Al Bait ALqadeem Restaurant and Cafe
listings.content: A traditional restaurant

listings.name: Al-Karmel Somali Restaurant
listings.content: East African cuisine

listings.name: Avon Restaurant
listings.content: An Indian Restaurant

listings.name: Africana Home Restaurant Nakheel Deira Park
listings.address: 1820, Lootah Building Behind Golden Square Hotel Street 118

listings.name: Al Dawaar Revolving Restaurant
listings.content: Serving an assortment of cuisines, the highlight of this beautiful restaurant is that it revolves, giving a nice tour of the city.
listings.price: Lunch: 185 dirhams per person, dinner: 235 dirhams per person

listings.name: Al Fanar Restaurant & Cafe
listings.content: Authentic Emirati cuisine, in the ambience of Dubai recreated from the 1960s.
listings.address: Canal Walk, Dubai Festival City Mall

listings.name: Kiku
listings.content: Japanese cuisine. Very high quality and very popular.

listings.name: Legends Steakhouse
listings.content: Part of the Creek Golf Clubhouse. The waterfront restaurant right on Dubai Creek is very popular with residents.

listings.name: Al Bait Alqadeem Restaurant & Cafe
listings.content: Emirati cuisine in an Emirati traditional house.
listings.address: Al Ahmadiya St crossing 15a St, Al Ras

listings.name: Floating Restaurants
listings.content: Tens of dhows propose a diner during a 2-hour cruise on the creek.
listings.address: Baniyas Rd, Al Sabkha & Al Rigga & Rigga Al Buteen communities

listings.name: JW's Steakhouse
listings.content: This is the Marriott's signature restaurant. Very popular with Dubai residents.

listings.name: Filli Cafeteria
listings.content: Probably the most popular tea spots in town, especially Filli, who serves over 4,000 cups a day. Try the zaffrani chai (milk tea with saffron) or the doodh kadak (strong milk tea).

listings.name: The Edge Pool & Bar
listings.content: Small bar but wonderful views especially at sunset.

listings.name: X Club
listings.content: Russia-themed bar.

listings.name: Dubai Youth Hostel
listings.content: Reception 24/7. Pool, football field, chill-out garden, A/C in the room, small bar fridge. It's located next to a mosque so morning prayers may wake you. Stadium metro station and bus stop just 100 m from hostel, Lulu Hyper Market shopping center and supermarket nearby. Free safety deposit boxes (hang on to your key as they have stiff US$200 replacement fee). Clean rooms but unhelpful staff. You can walk there from Terminal 2. When you get out walk straight along 16th St to the end. It takes around 10 min. From terminal 1 or 3 you can take the metro to Union and transfer to Green Line (just take a train on the other side of the platform) to Stadium station (zone 1 fare, 2 dirhams). A taxi from terminal 1 or 3 costs around 40 dirhams. It is a branch of the UAE YHA, and only hostel in Dubai; thus booked up weeks ahead. WiFi cost extra 10 dirhams.
listings.price: Dorm from 100 dirhams or US$27, breakfast included

listings.name: Gulf Pearl Hotel
listings.content: Rooms from 158 dirhams
listings.address: Al Baraha St, Omar al Khattab Rd

listings.name: Pacific Hotel
listings.content: Rooms from 300 dirhams or US$80.

listings.name: Niawara Guest House
listings.content: Probably one of the cheapest places in town.

listings.name: Alkhayam Hotel
listings.content: free wifi, nice cafe
listings.address: Sikkat Al Khali Street, PO box 88249

listings.name: Qasr Al Seyaha Hotel
listings.content: Another cheapy in the souk area

listings.name: Al Jazeera Hotel
listings.price: 220 dirhams dbl rm (200 dirhams if booked for 1 week)
listings.address: PO box 8814, Al Ahmadea Rd, Al Ras Area

listings.name: Galaxy Plaza
listings.content: 2-star place, a step up from the under-200-dirham places.

listings.name: Avari Dubai Hotel
listings.content: Rooms from US$152.

listings.name: Avenue Hotel
listings.content: Rooms start at 350 dirhams, including breakfast.

listings.name: Hyatt Regency Dubai
listings.content: 414 rooms and suites with views of the Persian Gulf. Host to Al Dawaar, Dubai's only revolving restaurant.

listings.name: InterContinental Residence Suites Dubai Festival City
listings.content: Offers one-, two- and three-bedroom serviced suites with a choice between Creek and city views. Available for short or long stays.

listings.name: Park Hyatt Dubai
listings.content: Waterfront location next to the Dubai Creek Golf and Yacht Club.

listings.name: Radisson Blu Hotel, Dubai Deira Creek
Taj Palace Hotel Dubai
listings.content: Near Naif Square Bazaar.

listings.name: Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood
listings.content: One of the last remaining pockets of Old Dubai, home to many reconstructed buildings in the traditional style. While information on the structures is slim here (see the museum in preference), the atmosphere is very evocative and there are plenty of delightful art galleries and cafes to explore.
listings.address: Al Fahidi (19th) St crossing ManKhool Rd, north-east of Al Souk Al Kabeer community

listings.name: Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding
listings.content: If you want to learn and understand the customs and traditions of UAE, this is the best place to go. The Centre hosts cultural meals for between 70 and 95 AED, with discussion of UAE culture, customs and religion. They run walking tours through the Bastakiya district for 60 minutes (35 AED) and 90 minutes (55 AED), starting at either 9 or 10:30AM daily except Friday.

listings.name: Creek Park
listings.content: A great place to hang out in the evening when the park is visited by people of different nationalities, all looking for calm place to enjoy the time. It has all the facilities of a modern park and is one of the best parks in Dubai. The cable car is closed.

listings.name: Dubai Dolphinarium
listings.content: The only indoor dolphinarium in the Middle East offers live shows of dolphins and seals. Swim with Dolphins is possible.
listings.image: Dolphin show at Dubai dolphinarium, September 2012.jpg

listings.name: Dubai Museum
listings.content: A must-see for anyone interested in the social history of the Emirate (and indeed the country). Located in and under al-Fahidi fort. The fort itself has a few examples of the traditional reed houses and other artifacts, but isn't much to look at. The more interesting parts are the modern galleries beneath the fort, showcasing Dubai's history using the latest technology and culminating in a reconstructed souq from the pearling days, complete with authentic sights and sounds. It is quite fascinating to see the speed at which the transition from poor pearling village to modern metropolis occurred.
listings.address: 11c Al Ibn Abi Talib St and 19 Al Fahidi St, Al Souk Al Kabeer community

listings.name: Grand Mosque
listings.content: Its large minaret is the imposing feature of this large mosque. It is popular for being quite close to a Hindu temple and one can see followers of both Islam and Hinduism gathering at the same place for prayers.
listings.address: Ali bin Ali Taleb (11C) St, Al Souk Al Kabeer community

listings.name: Heritage Village
listings.content: Home to the open museums of the Heritage and Diving Villages, and the houses of the late Sheikhs Saeed Al-Maktoum and Juma Al-Maktoum.

listings.name: Iranian mosque
listings.content: A very colourful and attractive tiled mosque; quite a contrast to the other much more plainly decorated mosques. Can be viewed from a carparking area off the north (creek) side of the street.
listings.address: Ali bin Abi Taleb (11C) St, Al Souk Al Kabeer community

listings.name: Sheikh Obaid bin Thani House
listings.content: a historic building home to royal family members built in 1916 and now converted into a museum. It provides good glimpse to old infrastructure of Dubai.

listings.name: Saeed Al Maktoum House
listings.content: Another very historic building built in 1894 now converted into a museum and contains artefacts and images of the old town of Dubai. It was the residence of the Saeed bin Maktoum bin Hasher Al Maktoum, the former ruler of Dubai.
listings.address: along the Dubai Creek in Al Shindagha

listings.name: Crossroad of Civilization Museum
listings.content: Museum includes a lot of artefacts and old books, including a Gutenberg Bible and a curtain of the door of Kaaba from 1543 AD.
listings.address: Sheikh Hasher bin Maktoum Al Maktoum Home, Al Mina Rd, Shindagha Heritage area, POBox 46298

listings.name: Old Weapons Museum
listings.content: Large collection of swords, daggers, riffles, from several centuries.

listings.name: Manuscript, Old Book and Print Museum
Zabeel Park
listings.content: The best and most popular park of town, it gives a remarkable glimpse of the desert and hot Dubai.
listings.address: Sheik Khalifa Bin Zayed St and Sheik Rashid Rd, Al Kefaf community

listings.name: Dubai Frame
listings.content: Two towers of 150 m height connected by a 100-m² bridge, the Dubai Frame has a museum and gallery where you can see the growth of Dubai from a simple fishing village to the ultra-modern city it is today with the use of photos and advanced technology. After visiting the museum, you take the elevator to the bridge to get a view of the city.

listings.name: Dubai Ferry trip
listings.content: The Dubai Ferry makes a sightseeing circular trip to Jumeirah Beach (deep sea side) or to the Floating Bridge (toward the creek). There are also a one way trips towards Dubai Marina at 1pm and 6pm (duration: 2 hours).
listings.price: 50 dirhams/person in regular, 75 dirhams/person in gold class
listings.address: Al Ghubaiba Marine Transport Station, Al Ghubaiba Rd, Al Shindagha community

listings.name: Gharana
listings.content: Gharana an Indian Restaurant in Holiday Inn Dubai – Al Barsha hotel brings you flavors of various spices and herbs with live entertainment.

listings.name: Basta Art Cafe
listings.content: Set in a lovely garden courtyard in a restored house. Great place to take a breather with a cold drink and write some postcards. The sandwiches-and-salads menu is aimed squarely at tourists, but if you are sick of kebabs, they will cater to your salmon-avocado wrap and mango smoothie cravings. The "Basta Special" drink of mint and lemon is also excellent.

listings.name: Gazebo
listings.content: Very nice and warm welcome given by the waiters. Food as good too. Not so expensive when compared to the quality of food.

listings.name: Ravi Restaurant
listings.content: A Pakistani restaurant that provides cheap Pakistani & Indian food. Good for anyone with a spicy tooth.

listings.name: Student Biryani
listings.content: A Pakistani restaurant serving the country's most popular biryani.

listings.name: Local House
listings.content: Emirati cuisine featuring camel meats and camel milkshakes in a traditional Dubai house.
listings.address: House 51, Al Fahidi Historical Neighbourhood, 19 Al Fahidi St, Al Souk Al Kabeer community

listings.name: Al Haj Bundu Khan
listings.content: Indian and Pakistani food.

listings.name: Pars Iranian Kitchen
listings.content: This is an open air Iranian restaurant where one can sit in traditional machans (large bed-like seating) and enjoy a fine Iranian meal. The speciality is the mixed grill which is served with live coal. After the meal, you may smoke a traditional sheesha pipe. No alcohol served.

listings.name: Wafi Gourmet
listings.content: Excellent Lebanese cuisine and ambience. In the cooler months the outdoor verandah is a pleasure. No alcohol served.

listings.name: Yakitori House
listings.content: Japanese cuisine, very popular with the Japanese expat community.
listings.address: Century Hotel, Khalid Bin Walid St, Bur Dubai

listings.name: Asha's
listings.content: Indian cuisine. Run by Asha Bosle. Good food but a little expensive

listings.name: Manhattan Grill
listings.content: Fine dining restaurant with New York-inspired cuisine, specialising in steak. A suitable venue for romantic dinners and family gatherings.

listings.name: Barrels Pub
listings.content: It is a bar is a clean, quiet and bright venue with large variates of snacks options. Every wall is mounted with screen playing number of sports games. The interiors looks good with polished timber tables and benches all around and wall cladding.

listings.name: Bollywood Café
listings.content: Excellent DJ, Live music and Indian food. It is a Bollywood-themed glamorous bar and nightlife with elegant to casual laid backs and pleasant musical twists, mostly Indian music.

listings.name: Chill Rooftop Lounge
listings.content: Dance floor with excellent DJ. It is an expansive rooftop venue painted in pink surrounded with fake grass. An outdoor seating place with good food.

listings.name: Marine's Club
listings.content: A lively bar and nightclub with 80s music most of the time. It is a budget friendly venue with great service and superb bouncers.

listings.name: Ascot Hotel
listings.content: Has Russian, Irish and Thai themed restaurants. Rooms from AED $180.

listings.name: Grand Hyatt Dubai
listings.content: A resort style hotel with extensive conference facilities and 13 restaurants serving cuisine from all over the world.

listings.name: Raffles Dubai
listings.content: Attached to Wafi Mall. Egyptian themed.

listings.name: Burj al-Arab
listings.content: This huge sail-shaped hotel completed in 1999 is a symbol of Dubai and its ascent in the world. The self-proclaimed world's first seven-star hotel (actually a five-star deluxe hotel) was the first icon of Dubai and still stands out on the skyline from its location on an artificial island 280 from the beach. Entry to the hotel is restricted to hotel guests, those with a restaurant reservation (minimum spend 200AED) or a guided tour (starting from 250AED for a 60-90min tour). A smart casual dress code applies but is not strictly enforced. Make restaurant reservations in advance.
listings.price: Overnight stays over US$1800 per night after taxes/fees

listings.name: Burj Khalifa
listings.content: At 828 m and 160 floors this is the world's tallest structure by a long shot, over 300 m taller than the previous contender in Taipei. The observation deck at the 124th floor is the second highest in the world after the Shanghai World Financial centre. Dominating the Dubai skyline, the tower houses a hotel and a Las Vegas-inspired fountain system. The visitors' entrance is at the lower ground floor of Dubai Mall. Although the tour is called At the Top, it isn't! At 452 m it's just over halfway up the tower itself. Console yourself with the knowledge that most of the rest of the tower consists of service areas and the view below looks suitably ant-like.
listings.price: Tickets cost 199 dirham for a timed-entry ticket, usually later the same day, or 400 dirham if you do not want to wait. The lines for tickets are often very long and at peak times, they can sell out several days in advance. It is strongly recommended to book tickets online ahead of your visit. For 500 dirham you can book a "SKY" ticket that includes a trip to level 148 of the building (which is relatively empty and exclusive) for 30 minutes, along with sweets and drinks. From there, you descend to the main observatory on levels 125 and 124 to join the masses waiting to go back down. The SKY ticket also includes a brief tour of the building's private areas. If you go for 'sunrise+breakfast' option for 140 dirham you can visit floor 124 at 05:30 and after, with floor 125 opening at 08:30 - this is a great way to avoid the queues and see the city during both night and day

listings.name: Dubai Fountain
listings.content: At 270m (900 ft) in length and sporting a jet that shoots water up to 150m (500 ft), it is the world's largest dancing fountain and one with a very enticing display - a definite must-see. It's most easily accessed via the Dubai Mall. There are private entranceways from the Burj Khalifa if you're staying there.

listings.name: Dubai Marina
listings.content: The Dubai Marina is to be the popular nightlife area of Dubai in the future. This multi-billion-dollar development is designed for tourists and water sport. The bars and cafés along the marina are popular gathering points for families and younger people. Most restaurants offer shisha and oriental food but food chains are fast entering too. The "Marina Walk" along the yachts is especially popular on Fridays and Saturdays. Yacht agencies offer services to explore the coastal region and Palm Islands.

listings.name: Jumeirah Beach
listings.content: Dubai is known for its great beaches and this one is the best. It's the most popular and busiest beach of the country. Expect to see swimmers in bikinis and ladies in abaya cloaks; this beach truly encapsulates the Westernisation of Dubai culture.

listings.name: Jumeirah Mosque
listings.content: The largest mosque in the city, and a wonderful example of Islamic architecture. It was built in the medieval Fatimid tradition with the interior decorated with elaborate Arabic calligraphy. It is one of few mosques in the city open for visits by non-Muslims; the Sheikh Mohammed Centre for Cultural Understanding conducts special tours for non-Muslims to help promote understanding of Islam. Guided tours are available on Tuesday, Thursday, and Sunday beginning at 10:00, followed by a question-and-answer session. The mosque is an especially great place to visit in the evening when it's dramatically illuminated by floodlights.

listings.name: Majlis Ghorfat Umm Al Sheif
listings.content: A restored traditional Emirati-style two story building used as a summer residence by Sheikh Rashid bin Saeed Al Maktoum, one of the founders of UAE, and father of the present ruler of Dubai.
listings.price: 1 dirham for adults and children over 6 years

listings.name: Palm Islands
listings.content: The Palm islands are the best symbols of the boom and bust construction cycles in Dubai. The "oldest" Palm called Palm Jumeirah is completed and is host to the gigantic Atlantis Hotel on its top. Several marinas, hotels and condo are along the palm leaves. Palm Jumeirah has the densest collection of beach clubs in the city, which are popular with locals and tourists alike. Some beach clubs are part of hotels, while others are standalone restaurants. West Beach falls in the latter category and is dog-friendly. The development of the other two Palms will depend on the financial situation of the construction business but someday Dubai will have the three largest artificial islands in the world on its coastline.

listings.name: Al Safa Park
listings.content: A beautiful planned park and one of the oldest parks in Dubai. It is a favourite for sports enthusiasts, and many visitors enjoy playing tennis, volleyball, and soccer. Children love playing games in the video arcade, or riding the Ferris wheel and bumper cars. The park even has a maze to wander through. Barbeques and picnic areas are available for those who want to make a day of it. It has lakes where you can take a boat ride and a hill that offers panoramic views of this beautiful lush green park and the gigantic Dubai skyline. But as of 2017, infrastructure are old disused and it have construction work.
listings.address: Al Hadiqa Rd, Al Safa community
listings.image: Downtown Burj Dubai and Business Bay, seen from Safa Park.jpg

listings.name: Etihad Museum
listings.content: Museum about the construction of the Union of the Emirates, after the withdrawal of British forces. Open in 2017, it features exhibits about the seven fathers, and the constitution. The Union House, where the treaty was signed, can be visited as well as the Guest Palace. It also hosts temporary exhibitions (e.g., philatelic in May 2017).
listings.address: 2nd December Rd crossing Jumeirah Rd, Jumeirah 1 community

listings.name: Dubai Aquarium and Underwater Zoo
listings.content: Giant aquarium, 51 long and 11 high. The visit includes a crossing inside the walk-through water tunnel, behind the scenes, and several other experiences. The Underwater Zoo has 140 fish species, desert animals, penguins and also hosts "King Krok". Animal feeding hours are indicated in the zoo, and it's also possible to participate during feeding.
listings.price: Researcher Experience for 100 dirham/person, Explorer Experience for 120 dirham/person, VIP for 300 dirham/person
listings.address: Dubai Mall, Doha St, Sheikh Zayed Rd

listings.name: Museum of the Future
listings.content: Branded as a "technology museum" many visitors consider it more of an expensive art exhibition. The building is outstanding though and looks particularly impressive in the dark.
listings.address: Emirates Towers, Sheikh Zayed Rd, Trade Center 2 community

listings.name: Jumeirah Fishing Harbor
listings.content: A quiet place with some nice restaurants.
listings.address: Jumeirah Rd crossing 311 Al Urouba Rd, Jumeirah 1 community

listings.name: The Lost Chambers Aquarium and Ambassador Lagoon
listings.content: An Atlantis-themed aquarium with a lot of fish species and jellyfishes. Don't miss the giant chamber with numerous sharks and rays. Shark feeding 10:15 and 15:45, ray feeding at 09:30 and 15:15. Possibilities to dive or do the "Aqua Trek" in the Ambassador Lagoon.
listings.price: 110 dirhams/adult, 80 dirham/child below 11, discounts for UAE residents, 30 dirham for Ambassador Lagoon only
listings.address: Atlantis, Cresent Rd East, Palm Jumeirah

listings.name: Dubai Miracle Garden
listings.content: A coloful and well maintained garden with more than 45 million flowers and numerous sculptures made out of flowers. Some visitors found it a bit too kitschy.

listings.name: Emirates Towers
listings.content: The Emirates Towers complex contains the Emirates Office Tower and Jumeirah Emirates Towers Hotel. The two towers, which rise to 355 m (1,165 ft) and 309 m (1,014 ft), respectively, stand as the 23rd and 47th tallest buildings in the world. The two towers are connected by a 9,000 m² (96,875 ft²) two-storey retail complex known as "The Boulevard". The Emirates Towers complex is located on the Sheikh Zayed Road in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and is a symbol of the city of Dubai. A curiosity of the design is that the towers have a similar number of floors; the taller office tower actually contains 54 floors, while the hotel tower contains 56 floors. This is because the individual floor heights of the office tower are greater than that of the hotel. The Emirates Towers complex is set in over 570,000 m² (42 acres) of gardens, with lakes, waterfalls and public seating areas. There is parking space for up to 1,800 cars.

listings.name: The View at The Palm
listings.content: Observation deck, 5-star hotel, luxury apartments. See the spectacular views over Palm Jumeirah.

listings.name: Sky Views Dubai
listings.content: This hotel building offers beautiful views toward Burj Khalifa from its 53rd floor observation deck. There is a 25-m glass floor walk and a ride on a glass slide included. For another dirham a walk along the edge of this building floor can be booked.
listings.address: Sky Views, Sheikh Mohammed bin Rashid Blvd

listings.name: Cycling or walking along Jumeirah Beach
listings.content: A beautiful coastal running and cycling track stretches for about 7 km from the mouth of Dubai Canal all the way to Burj Al Arab. One of the few places in Dubai where you can see native Emiratis enjoying their time alongside expats from all over the world in the evenings. There are bike rental stations along the way (mobile data and a credit card needed though).

listings.name: Ski Dubai
listings.content: Dubai has a snow skiing centre in the Mall of the Emirates, offering both skiing and snowboarding. The 400 slope is quite large for an indoor area. All equipment is available for hire. Although it is -4 inside, you do not need to bring a jacket because they supply pretty much everything except gloves and a hat which you can buy right there (gloves are included in some packs). It also propose the "Penguin Encounter" activity where you interact and play with penguins (king and gentoo).
listings.price: A "Slope Session" pass costs 200 dirhams for 2 hours or 300 dirhams for full day, plus 20 dirhams, for a locker. The "Snow Park" starts at 190 dirhams, the pack with all activities unlimited "Ski Dubai Experience" costs 500 dirhams
listings.address: Mall of Emirates, Sheikh Zayed Rd crossing Umm Suqueim Rd, Al Barsha 1

listings.name: Wild Wadi Waterpark
listings.content: The perfect place for the entire family to spend a day as well as being a great way to beat the heat and enjoy the day away from the bustle of the city. Located close to the hotels and resorts of Jumeriah Beach, the park has water rides, slides, and a lagoon that is hidden away. You'll enjoy waterfalls, out of the way swimming holes, and a tidal pool.

listings.name: Atlantis
listings.content: Atlantis-themed but Arabian-styled resort on the artificial island of The Palm. Has a huge water park with plenty of thrilling water slides, an aquarium and a large shopping area with plenty of places to eat and drink.

listings.name: Aquaventure Waterpark
listings.content: Aquaventure have a lot of water slides, including the extreme slides: Leap of feath and Poseidon's Revenge. It also includes Dolphin encounter, swimming with dolphins. The waterpark also contains the Dubai Balloon, which offers 10min balloon rides up to 300m high for AED 175 (adults) and AED 75 (children).
listings.price: 320 dirham/adults 275 dirham/child under 1.2, 40 dirhams for locker, discounts via online booking
listings.address: Atlantis, Cresent Rd East, Palm Jumeirah

listings.name: Skydive Dubai
listings.content: Tandem jumps over the Palm Jumeirah or the desert. Gyrocopter flights available as well.

listings.name: Megaplex
listings.content: Experience the next generation of cinemas and impressive effects in the Middle East. You can also book tickets via app or online.

listings.name: Dubai Marina Yacht Club
listings.content: A quiet and peaceful place with colorful lights at the night. You can rent a boat for a few hours or a day or just sit there for hours watching the skyscrapers and eating out at great restaurants.

listings.name: XLine
listings.content: The world's longest urban zip line.

listings.name: 800 Pizza
listings.content: Traditional & authentic Italian pizza baked in wood fired Italian stone oven, thin & crispy crust.

listings.name: More Cafe
listings.content: Serves breakfast, lunch and light continental and oriental meals. Good service and big portions.

listings.name: Noodle House
listings.content: Asian food.
listings.address: Emirates Towers Shopping Blvd, Madinat Jumeirah

listings.name: Chill Out
listings.content: Have a delicious contemporary European food in ice lounge at a chilling temperature of -6. It is first of its kind in the Middle East. From tables to even crockery in which food is served, all made of ice.
listings.address: Times Square Centre, Ground F, Sheihk Zayed Rd, Al Marabea St, Al Quoz community

listings.name: Chimes
listings.content: Thai, Singaporean, Malaysian and Indonesian themed food, and the popular house speciality must be the pepper or chili crab. You can eat at the restaurant or order home delivery to most areas of new Dubai.

listings.name: Jedoudna Restaurant
listings.content: A family-run Lebanese restaurant. With outdoor seating and separate shisha area.
listings.address: Rimal Sector, The Walk at Jumeirah Beach Residence

listings.name: Karam Beirut
listings.content: Excellent Lebanese food.
listings.address: 1st floor, Mall of Emirates, Sheykh Zayed Rd, Al Barsha

listings.name: Lal Qila Dubai
listings.content: Pakistani cuisine.

listings.name: London Fish & Chips
listings.content: Fish, chips, sharky meals, traditional battered, baked potatoes, sandwiches, salads and soups
listings.address: Tunisia Food Court, Ibn Batutta Mall, Jebel Ali Village

listings.name: Toscana
listings.content: Italian.

listings.name: Al Fresco
listings.content: Specialized in Italian food with cosy outdoor seating. Business lunch, Family friendly place. Smoking and alcohol is permitted. Try the garlic bruschetta with traditional tomato, the leafy green salad, oozy burrata cheese, tomato, sprinkled with drizzles of balsamic vinegar.
listings.address: Crowne Plaza, Dubai, Sheikh Zayed Road

listings.name: Al Mahara
listings.content: Part of the Burj Al Arab hotel, and as you would expect is also very high quality, especially seafood.

listings.name: At.mosphere
listings.content: Exclusive fine dining restaurant on Level 122 of Burj Khalifa.

listings.name: The Gem Garden
listings.content: Continental restaurant.
listings.address: Holiday Inn Dubai - Al Barsha, Sheikh Zayed Road

listings.name: Gharana
listings.content: Authentic Indian restaurant.
listings.address: Holiday Inn Dubai - Al Barsha, Sheikh Zayed Road

listings.name: Margaux
listings.content: European, steak and continental cuisine. Pleasing and stunning ambiance with variations and one could enjoy the views of Burj Khalifa and the fountain shows.
listings.address: Souk al Bahar, opp dubai mall fountains

listings.name: Options, by Sanjeev Kapoor
listings.content: Run by famed Indian TV chef Sanjeev Kapoor. Drinks served. Reservations recommended especially on Friday nights.

listings.name: The Royal Budha
listings.content: Authentic Thai restaurant.
listings.address: Holiday Inn Dubai - Al Barsha, Sheikh Zayed Road

listings.name: Shang Palace
listings.content: Good Chinese food. No smoking
listings.address: Level 1, Shangri-La Hotel, Shk Zayed Rd

listings.name: Al Nafoorah
listings.content: Arabic, Lebanese and Middle Eastern cuisines. Outdoor seating with perfect sense of fine dining accompanied with comfortable, Arabian-style terrace. Smoking and alcohol is permitted.
listings.address: Jumeirah, Emirates Towers Boulevard, Sheikh Zayed Road

listings.content: Jumeirah Beach Hotel Complex. Open air bar with great views of the Burj hotel and the Jumeirah beach hotel all helped by a cool breeze from the ocean. Various DJs but think Ibiza lounge bar and you will not be far off.

listings.name: Buddha Bar
listings.content: Branch of the international Asian-themed bar/restaurant. Full of crowds.
listings.address: Grosvenor House Dubai, Al Sufouh Rd

listings.name: Barasti
listings.content: Built in three levels (each playing its own music), with lounging areas on the beach, lots of young and foreign people come here during the weekend. Very popular with expats.

listings.name: Nasimi Beach
listings.content: Great bar/club on the beach in the Palm Jumeirah.

listings.name: Long's Bar
listings.content: The longest bar in the UAE, typical English style with live football, similar to a UK Wetherspoons. Great music and DJs plus food and friendly atmosphere.

listings.name: Left Bank
listings.content: O the waterfront in one of the most tranquil areas of Dubai. A great food menu leads on to some excellent cocktails and music inside.

listings.name: Observatory
listings.content: Bar and restaurant with great view across Palm Jumeirah (on a clear day!) Popular happy hour with the after work crowd on Thursday from 18:00-20:00.

listings.name: Skyview Bar
listings.content: Live local and international bands, reservations are a must.

listings.name: Vu's Bar
listings.content: Try the 51st Floor house cocktail, it's so deliciously strong, also there's a staggering 200 cocktails to choose from.

listings.name: Zero Gravity
listings.content: Beach club, a nice place for partying.

listings.name: VIP Room
listings.content: It is a lounge-like lively space that offers mid-range to high-price drinks. The huge multi-color circular space is cornered by large LCD screens and exclusive tables and the scantily clad podium dancers.
listings.address: JW Marriott, Marquis Hotel Dubai, Sheikh Zayed Road

listings.name: The Act
listings.content: This venue is full of dance artists, mischievous performances, women performing unusual stunts and on-stage antics. It is a place where you will forget that you are in Dubai. The drinks are good and are slightly over priced but this place will make you feels liberated, little bit different and edgy.

listings.name: The Cigar Bar
listings.content: Specialized in true cigar aficionado, cognacs and whiskies. Smoking is permitted. Dresscode is smart casuals. It is a traditional venue with modern rich dark enveloping and mahogany lined interior furnishing. The Cigar Bar will be closed during the Holy Month of Ramadan

listings.name: Zinc
listings.content: It is the city’s most popular nightclubs with girls night out, dance floor and variety of DJ sets. This place is always over crowded and the drinks are budget friendly.
listings.address: Crowne Plaza Dubai, Sheikh Zayed Road

listings.name: The Address Downtown Dubai
listings.content: One of the many luxury hotels next to Burj Khalifa with many good fine dining restaurants and bars.
listings.address: Mohammed Bin Rashid Boulevard, Downtown Dubai

listings.name: Anantara The Palm Dubai Resort
listings.content: Houses the only over water villas in the UAE.

listings.name: Atlantis, the Palm
listings.content: Hotel on the Palm. Connects to mainland by monorail.

listings.name: Fairmont Dubai
listings.content: Closest 5-star hotel to the World Trade Centre.

listings.name: Fraser Suites Dubai
listings.content: Serviced apartments and accommodation.
listings.address: Sidra Tower, Sheikh Zayed Road, Media City

listings.name: Hilton Dubai Jumeirah
listings.content: Resort with a private beach. The hotel is only 10 floors which is dwarfed by nearby high-rises, but the location is lively and the pool/garden area is lush.
listings.address: Tower A, The Walk, Jumeirah Beach Residence

listings.name: Holiday Inn Dubai - Al Barsha
listings.content: 310 elegant rooms, a choice of 3 bars, choice of 2 fine dining restaurants and 6-storey high atrium and piano lounge. Gymnasium, roof top pool, massage rooms, sauna and spa.

listings.name: Jumeirah Beach Hotel
listings.content: Next to Burj al-Arab and run by the same company.

listings.name: The Radisson Blu Residence, Dubai Marina
listings.content: 5 km away from Jafza, and economic free zone. It has 152 apartments with scenic balcony, two restaurants with the convenience of onsite dining. They arrange variety of events from time to time.
listings.address: Plot No. 392-260 Street K Dubai Marina

listings.name: Chelsea Gardens Hotel Apartments
listings.content: It has 169 well-appointed luxury comfortable and spacious apartment suites with modern interior. Upon request, they offer airport transfers.

listings.name: Emirates Grand Hotel
listings.content: It is a non-alcoholic hotel decorated with luxurious amenities. Equipped with stream rooms, hot tubs, sauna, roof top pool, fitness center and tennis court.
listings.address: Near Finance Centre, Metro Stop, Sheikh Zayed Road

listings.name: Dusit Thani Dubai
listings.content: Beautiful surroundings with Asian hospitality and teak-wood furniture all around and Venetian blinds. champagne lounge available. They have 321 modern rooms equipped with high-speed Internet connections.

listings.name: Holiday Inn Dubai - Al Barsha
listings.content: 4-star hotel.
listings.address: Near Mall of The Emirates, E11 Sheikh Zayed Rd

listings.name: Hilton Dubai Al Habtoor City
listings.content: The hotel is 44 floors and has 1004 guest rooms, 8 dining outlets and 21 meeting rooms. 10 minutes by car from Downtown Dubai.
listings.address: Al Habtoor City, Sheikh Zayed Road

listings.name: Th8 Palm Dubai Beach Resort
listings.content: Beachfront resort.

listings.name: Anantara World Islands Dubai Resort
listings.content: Beachfront resort located on the World Islands. Contains a Swimming pool, spa, Paddle court, Fitness centre, Water sports centre, Kids’ club and Games room

listings.name: The Heart of Europe
listings.content: Complex of several European-themed hotels spanning six islands in the Europe section of the World Islands. Includes Spanish-themed Marbella resort, four French Riviera-themed hotels (complete with marketplace and discotheque), Italian-themed Portofino Hotel, British-inspired Hotel London, Artist Hotel, the Danish-style Hygge Hotel, the Sweden Beach house, and 133 floating villas

listings.name: Port of Jebel Ali
listings.content: The world's largest man-made harbour and the biggest port in the Middle East. It was constructed in the late 1970s to supplement the facilities at Port Rashid. It is located thirty-five kilometres southwest of Dubai, in the Persian Gulf. On April 9, 2011 Jebel Ali Port won the Golden Award for Best Seaport Overall from the Higher Committee for UAE Civil Seaports and Airports Security.

listings.name: Jebel Ali Shooting Club
listings.content: This club has awesome architecture and design. It has wide range of shooting options to practice right from automatic ball trap, Olympic trap, down the line, Olympic skeet to compak sporting.

listings.name: Switch Bowling
listings.content: A multi-lane bowling section, one of the perfect indoor entertainment venue for families and kids. In addition, it has billiards section, video gaming areas, toddlers' play area and restaurants.

listings.name: Peekaboo!
listings.content: An ideal place for children below 7 years, for entertaining and creative activities. There is a variety of play equipment, toys and classes for kids.

listings.name: Seawings
listings.content: Experience live areal views and sightseeing excursions of Dubai's modern skyline and dazzling landmarks. The water-based take-offs and landings further adds greater experience.

listings.name: Jetty Lounge
listings.content: This is an elegant beach lounge that has fantastic drinks. Cozy, but over-crowded during the sunsets.

listings.name: Oasis Town of Dahid
listings.content: Explore the village, its traditions and the oasis.

listings.name: Dubai Parks & Resorts
listings.content: Dubai Parks and Resorts is the Middle East's largest integrated leisure and theme park destination featuring more than 100 rides and attractions, and consists of three theme parks: Motiongate Dubai, Bollywood Parks Dubai, and Legoland Dubai, and one water park: Legoland Water Park. It also encompasses Riverland Dubai, which is a themed retail and dining destination, as well as the Polynesian-themed family resort, Lapita Hotel Dubai.

listings.name: Jebel Ali Club
listings.content: A good restaurant with relaxing pub, pools, darts, swimming pool and steam rooms. The drink and food is budget friendly.
listings.address: Old Jabel Ali Village, Near Ibn Battuta Mall (Sheikh Zayed Rd), Dubai

listings.name: The Kebab Shop
listings.content: Good budget friendly food specialized in British, Pakistani, Indian and Turkish food

listings.name: Kcal Healthy Fast Food
listings.content: Healthy fast food and great dining experience.

listings.name: Chicken Tikka Inn
listings.content: Awesome place for great Indian food.

listings.name: La Fontana
listings.content: Mediterranean cuisine, generous breakfast buffet, international dishes and a variety of themed dinner buffets, either indoors or on the large outdoor terrace.
listings.address: JA Palm Tree Court, Ground Floor, next to the La Fontana Swimming Pool

listings.name: Mushref Bar
listings.content: Shaded by palm trees with numerous pool bars, entertainment zones and sunbeds.
listings.address: JA Jebel Ali, Beach Hotel, Jebel Ali

listings.name: Palmito Pool Bar
listings.content: Swim-up pool bar serving good drinks and refreshments.
listings.address: JA Palm Tree Court, Jebel Ali, Dubai

listings.name: Sunset Lounge
listings.content: Great Beverages.
listings.address: JA Jebel Ali Beach Hotel, Jebel Ali

listings.name: Diablo Nightclub Dubai
listings.content: It is a Moroccan Themed lounge that serves cocktails, shisha, teas and coffees.
listings.address: Ibn Battuta Gate Hotel in Jebel Ali

listings.name: The Bar
listings.content: Casual lounge with indoor and al fresco seating. It serves beverages, cocktails, light snacks and light dishes.
listings.address: Courtyard by Marriott Dubai Green Community

listings.name: Jebel Ali Beach Hotel
listings.content: Pets are not allowed. Speaks Russian, English, German and Arabic. This luxurious resort hotel is located on the Arabian Gulf. It has 1km private beach surrounded by palm trees and sun loungers. All the rooms are bright and stylish and they have fresh air and scenic balcony.
listings.address: Exit 13, Sheikh Zayed Road, Jebel Ali, Dubai

listings.name: Premier Inn Dubai Investments Park Hotel
listings.content: This hotel offers, business services, multilingual staff, free wi-fi, Video Conferencing, night clubs, casinos, safe deposit box and swimming pool.

listings.name: Mushrif Park
listings.content: Mushrif Park is 5.25-km² (1300-acre) desert-like park. It is in the eastern part of the city (near the suburb of Khawaneej), about 16 km (10 mi) from the traditional center of Dubai. The park was created in early 1980 by Dubai Municipality and was hugely expanded and refurbished in 1989.
listings.price: entrance fee 10 dirhams per car; to use the swimming pool, adults pay 10 dirhams and children pay 5 dirhams

listings.name: Imagine
listings.content: Plays two different big water, fire and light shows: Stardancer and A Child's Dream. Have several world records.
listings.address: Festival Bay, Dubai Festival City, Festival Blvd

listings.name: Global Village
listings.content: Annual festival (usually during winter). Countries around the world gather and set up a small village in the outskirts of Dubai. Each country/region has its own pavilion with a unique replica of their famous landmarks. This is usually like a flea market where you can get souvenirs from almost every corner of the earth for a bargained price and experience as if you're in that certain country for at least 10 minutes of your life even if you're 10,000 km away. Raffles for cars and gold bars also happen. You'd see the hieroglyphics of Egypt, temples of Thailand, Forbidden City of Beijing, the Eiffel Tower and many more.
listings.address: Exit #37 on Sh Mohammed Bin Zayed Rd

listings.name: Dubai Autodrome
listings.content: This is 5-km world-class motorsports circuit hosted many international championships. You can take thrilling driving experience here in some of the world's fastest sports cars.

listings.name: IMG Worlds of Adventure
listings.content: A very large indoor theme park, with 4 universes: Lost Valley, IMG boulverard, Cartoon Network, Marvell. Nice families and adventurers, specially during hot summer months. It has 22 attractions including 3 roller coasters: The Velociraptor (5 inversions), Predator (3 inversions) and Spiderman (turning seats).
listings.address: City of Arabia, Sheikh Mohammed bin Zayed Rd E311

listings.name: Dubai Sports City (DSC)
listings.content: A 50-million square feet mixed use development that will be the world’s first integrated purpose-built sports city. The development is being built around five major sports venues and features a series of major sports academy facilities. It contains these sporting complexes:

listings.name: DSC Multi-Purpose Stadium
listings.content: The main sports structure will be a 60,000-seat multi-purpose outdoor stadium. This stadium will be used for athletics, cricket and football.

listings.name: Dubai International Stadium
listings.content: A 25,000-seat cricket stadium, popularly known as Ring of Fire.

listings.name: DSC Indoor Arena
listings.content: A 10,000-seat indoor arena.

listings.name: Rugby Park
listings.content: A 5,000-seat field hockey stadium. The stadium will provide a base to the UAE Hockey Committee and the WorldHockey Academy. The Hockey Stadium is situated at the Dubai Sports City Academy's Campus and provides world-class facilities for international athletes and local enthusiasts. The World Hockey Academy is the first facility of its kind anywhere in the world. Through a partnership between Dubai Sports City and the International Hockey Federation, the World Hockey Academy will provide coaching at the highest professional level from seasoned hockey coaches, many of whom have represented their countries in the international arena.

listings.name: Dubai Safari Park
listings.content: Dubai Safari Park is a wildlife park, animal sanctuary & education center that is home to more than 2,500 animals from all over the world including lions, elephants, giraffes, moon bears, and camels. The park is divided into four zones - Explorer Village, African Village, Arabian Desert Safari, and Asian Village.

listings.name: Al Mallah
listings.content: Amazing food. It is popular for casual dining, juices, sandwiches and fast food. A good place to visit along with family and friends.

listings.name: Sidra
listings.content: Specialized in Arabic, Lebanese and Middle Eastern Foods. This spacious alfresco area is bigger than other restaurants, full of shrubs and bushes with two distinct large indoor spaces - smokers and non-smokers. It is open for post party up to 4am.

listings.name: InterContinental Dubai Festival City
listings.content: 498 rooms over 36 floors with views of the Dubai Creek and a 3800-m² event centre. Attached to the Festival Centre shopping mall.

listings.name: The Meydan Hotel
listings.content: Stylish hotel with 285 furnished rooms. It is equipped with rooftop pool, fitness center, spas, recreations centers like tennis and target shooting games. Its restaurant is specialized in steaks, Italian and Asian cuisine. Ladies-only units are also available.
listings.address: Meydan Racecourse, Al Meydan Road, Nad Al Sheba

listings.name: Hotel ibis
listings.content: Located on Sheikh Zayed Road, next to Ski Dubai & Mall of the Emirates. This mid-range hotel has 204 cozy air-conditioned with bathtubs. Equipped with Italian restaurant, coffee shop and bar. Private indoor parking available.
listings.price: 129 dirham for a room with a double bed

listings.name: Studio One
listings.content: A hotel in Studio City with many great restaurants (including Italian, Mexican, and Irish cuisine). The rooms are filled with modern art-y decor, as is the lobby. It also has a pool.
listings.price: 151 dirham per night for a single room, however can be up to 900 depending on time of year

listings.name: Dubai Youth Hostel
listings.content: Clean budget hotel that offers private double rooms with comfortable beds with air conditioning. Equipped with swimming pool and good food restaurant.
